# Data-plane callback optimization review

Status: in progress. Anchor: `edgion-gateway`. Baseline: `81291f899`.

Review callbacks and their reachable data-plane work incrementally. Apply only
behavior-preserving optimizations through IMPL plan and final independent review,
verify each batch, and commit separately without pushing. Deferred proposals need
the user's decision. This directory follows the user's explicit singular `task/`
destination.

## TCP/TLS connection and relay review

No production change selected in this batch. TCP retains its selected route unit
rather than the whole route table across I/O, and owns its formatted upstream
address in the log context.

would need separate behavioral/performance evidence; none is proposed here.

reduced in the following batch. CN validation still uses the full canonical

## Quota internal UUID stack encoding

Credential reservation and identity/model quota admission now encode their
internal UUID into the uuid crate's stack buffer instead of constructing a
temporary String. Locked uuid 1.24.0 Simple Display uses the same lowercase
encoding, preserving the 32-byte unhyphenated representation. Random generation
stays after Redis-client health checks; each invocation still generates one ID,
shared by every target in that quota admission.

Both canonical Redis key builders synchronously hash the ID and return owned
key strings. The buffer is not retained by a lease or Redis future. Window IDs,
cluster-slot hashing, request-marker isolation, TTLs, admission and failure
policies are unchanged. This removes the intermediate formatting String in each
path; key storage and RNG work remain. Existing quota, attempt and shared Redis
core tests provide verification without duplicating the UUID library tests.

## Quota window millisecond precomputation

CompiledLimit now stores the private u128 window_ms value computed once from
parsed Duration with the same as_millis().max(1) normalization. Target building
reads that value instead of repeating conversion and normalization for every
limit on every admission. Clock capture, division/remainder, u128 identity bytes,
window ID conversion and retention/retry durations are unchanged.

The existing bucket-boundary regression now obtains its limits through the real
quota compiler, verifying that 1m still rotates at 60,000 milliseconds and keeps
the one-millisecond remainder before the boundary. Other scope, identity and
reorder tests keep their original inputs with explicit millisecond fields.
This is configuration-only precomputation, not a new runtime policy, storage-size
claim or measured throughput improvement.

## Redis quota and reservation integer arguments

Cumulative quota admission/update and credential reservation now pass validated
i64 arguments to the same generic script executor, extending the ordinary
rate-limit argument optimization. This removes seven intermediate decimal Strings
from each quota invocation and five from each credential-reservation invocation.
Every u64 conversion follows its existing Lua exact-integer validation at
2^53 - 1, including limits, TTLs, revision and cumulative/credential amounts.
Absent optional credential limits remain zero; operation codes and final flags
retain their existing signed integer values.

Locked Fred 10.1.0 uses integer-as-bulk/blob encoding in both RESP command codecs;
redis-protocol 6.0.0 writes the same decimal argument bytes as the previous string
values. Lua bodies, keys, argument order, result parsing and exact NOSCRIPT-only
fallback are unchanged. Container cloning and command buffers still allocate;
this is not an allocation-free Redis operation or a throughput claim. Existing
boundary, TTL, quota and reservation tests cover the retained policy checks.

## Quota worker ownership and future-layout audit

Inspected the complete quota accumulator/worker lifecycle and its Redis sink.
Context, worker and response processor retain separate accumulator owners;
notifications carry no accounting payload, so monotonic atomic watermarks remain
the source of truth. Attempted high-water is recorded before await to avoid
refunding uncertain applies. Final retry deadlines, lease refresh, request-drop
abort, timeout abort and completed-worker joining retain independent purposes.
No clone was removed from these cross-task owners.

The per-flush boxed future is a candidate, but generic direct dispatch changes
the persistent worker layout. Allocation and idle-residency consequences need
measurement before it qualifies as impact-free. The decision and acceptance
criteria are in [quota-01](quota-01-worker-future-representation.md). No runtime,
trait, test or parallel-target behavior changed in this audit.

## Credential reservation limiter borrowing

Credential admission now borrows the limiter owned by AiAttemptAdmissionInput
through the existing Redis await. It clones the same Arc only when a Reserved
or Duplicate result constructs a settlement lease. The input already remains
alive across this operation, and RedisRateLimiter neither inspects reference
counts nor owns a custom destructor. Rejected, failed, timed-out or cancelled
operations no longer acquire and release the redundant limiter Arc. Successful
leases retain the same ownership needed for later settlement.

Client lookup, UUID/key generation, limits, TTL, timeout, Redis invocation and
result mapping are unchanged. Cancellation still leaves uncertain remote charges
to the existing conservative TTL policy. This is a reference-count optimization;
no throughput, allocation or async-frame-size improvement was measured.

## Quota target identity scratch reuse

build_targets now clears and reuses one local byte buffer across quota limits
instead of allocating a fresh identity buffer per limit. Capacity is requested
lazily inside the iterator, so empty input does not allocate identity scratch.

shared key builder still produces independent owned bucket/marker strings.
The buffer is released when synchronous target construction returns, before
Redis admission awaits. Clock capture, deadlines, limits and target order remain
unchanged. No hash/key format, shared key API or response-body ownership changed.

The existing mixed-scope/reordering regression now compares each combined target
with an independent single-target build, including both bucket and marker keys.
Reversed IdentityModel/Identity ordering verifies that prior model bytes do not
leak into the next identity. This reuses temporary capacity across limits; no
fixed allocation count or measured throughput gain is claimed.

## Provider cooldown Retry-After borrowing

upstream response instead of creating a temporary String. Attempt/outlier
handling synchronously parses it into Duration and stores only numeric cooldown
state. The borrow ends before the original header is removed and any accepted
normalized delta-seconds value is inserted.

evaluation, cooldown precedence and header mutation order remain unchanged.
This removes the temporary copy for eligible nonempty values; normalized output
and other downstream work can still allocate. No throughput improvement or
allocation-free cooldown path is claimed.

## Unchanged reported-usage publication

observe_reported_usage now compares the fully normalized next value with the
current optional snapshot and publishes a new Arc only when they differ. The
private ArcSwap remains the sole immutable multi-field publication owner; readers
receive copied values and no consumer depends on repeated store notifications
or Arc identity. Production writers remain sequential response processors.

gate retain their order. None still differs from an initial all-zero reported
snapshot. Separate accounting_snapshot reads and quota notifications are unchanged.
The new allocation regression covers repeated zero, identical and lower snapshots,
then invalid merged cache detail clearing an existing valid detail and repeating
that normalized result. Unchanged warmed observations allocate no new snapshot;
changed observations still publish normally. No concurrency-policy or throughput
improvement is claimed.

## SSE literal comparison without materialization

SliceChain now compares a validated range with a literal through its canonical
borrowed fragment walker. SseEventRef uses it for event_is and its existing
single-data-line literal check. Native Messages classifies its four recognized
event names through event_is, avoiding temporary strings when names span slices;
canonical Chat DONE checks similarly avoid materializing fragmented data.

Matching a valid string literal also guarantees valid UTF-8 for that match.
Case sensitivity, missing versus empty names, duplicate-name selection, the
single-data-line requirement and poisoned-block policies remain unchanged.
The helper rejects reversed/out-of-bounds ranges before visiting storage.
No decoding, coalescing, retained-byte bounds or event ownership was changed.

Regressions compare decoder checks with the prior materializing expressions at
every two-way split, including empty/missing, repeated, mixed-case and invalid
UTF-8 names and multiline data. Chain tests cover sliced/coalesced storage,
empty/invalid ranges and late mismatches. Comparisons allocate zero bytes in
these tests; classification may traverse fragments more than once, so no general
CPU or throughput improvement is claimed.

## Bounded attempt identity ownership

Admission and terminal ledger construction now consume backend and credential
identity strings. The shared local helper transfers a String only when its length
is within the existing field bound and its capacity equals its length; otherwise
it uses the existing UTF-8-safe bounded copy. This avoids retaining spare capacity
or truncating a larger allocation in place. Reservation still sees the full alias
before any log-field bounding.

All four ledger callers own a removed mutable active attempt. Only the two identity
fields are taken; snapshot evaluation stays first, and later accounting, reservation
and adaptive operations do not read these fields. The independent plan review
identified this narrow transfer as safe without a borrowed admission API or a
change to the captured-generation lifetime.

Differential tests cover empty strings, spare-capacity empty strings, short/exact/
over-limit values and multibyte boundaries. Accepted transfer cases preserve the
buffer pointer and perform zero allocations; all cases match the previous output
and requested String capacity. This does not claim physical allocator size or
measured throughput improvements.

## Borrowed resolver address fingerprints

HTTPDNS borrows the prepared generation's redacted address identity, and standard
DNS retains the exact owned formatting. Gateway's existing resolver owner keeps

Path and form-query binding now pass their decoded Cow<str> into scalar conversion.
String, bytes, enum and validated 64-bit integer text move an existing owned
String into the bound JSON value; borrowed text still receives an owned copy.
Numeric parsing, error ordering and original integer spelling are preserved.
BoundRequest retains independent ownership after input buffers leave scope.

The baseline-first scalar regression covers borrowed and owned forms across all
scalar families, integer boundaries and malformed values. A separate escaped-path
regression verifies pointer and capacity identity for the moved string-producing
families. This establishes buffer transfer, not measured throughput or RSS gains.
Decoder spare capacity remains retained; the owning conversion memory ledger now
explicitly accounts for it under the unchanged encoded input cap and existing
selector/scratch allowance. No exact-capacity equivalence is claimed. Strict query
preflight remains unchanged; grpc-01 still requires a separate decision.

## gRPC codec descriptor handoff

Request encoding now borrows one method input descriptor for normalization and
moves that same handle into DynamicMessage deserialization. Response decoding
likewise borrows one output descriptor for wire admission and moves it into
DynamicMessage decoding. Descriptor acquisition remains after the existing
profile or response-byte checks, and admission still precedes reflection.

The locked prost-reflect implementation builds these handles from a pool Arc and
an index. Each path reaching reflection avoids one redundant descriptor handle
clone/drop; this is not a descriptor-data copy, heap-allocation or throughput
claim. The binding already pins the pool across the request serialization interval.
JSON-tree release, capped writers, panic containment, output envelopes and memory
reservations remain unchanged. Existing ownership, malformed-input/wire, limits,
WKT and round-trip regressions cover this local handoff without new mirrored tests.

## WAF response completion reachability

The only Gateway call to execute_response_window is WafPlugin's completion hook,
which passes an empty terminal window. There is no Gateway response-chunk feed
to that leaf API. Positive/non-excluded RESPONSE_BODY targets are classified as
unavailable FullResponseBody and rejected by strict compilation; support reports
do not authorize publication. The leaf API's nonempty-window capability is not
evidence that the Gateway uses it on streamed response chunks.

For the current empty window, owned_copy creates an empty Vec, reserves zero and
extends an empty slice. There is no payload allocation to remove at that site.
This does not imply that phase execution, matchers or outcome summaries allocate
nothing. Completion claims the selected owner's phase, moves its transaction out,
executes phase four and then logging, and does not reinstall the transaction.
Logging still executes after a successful phase-four intervention; only a runtime
error returns early. The final intervention prefers phase four via Option::or.
Owner mismatch and duplicate claims skip execution. These ownership and ordering
boundaries were retained, not optimized away.

Direct WAF completion wiring is inspected; deeper engine operators and full
response-chain coverage remain open. This documentation-only batch passed
independent plan review and fresh serial tests: 50 Gateway WAF, four leaf response
and 33 Resources WAF tests. Formatting and workspace check/Clippy passed with
existing unrelated warnings. No live transport or performance benchmark ran.

## Transcoder terminal outcome lock

GrpcTranscodingPlan::finalize_log now normalizes Pending to Interrupted and
publishes the existing terminal log under one outcome lock. The shared private
transition also serves response cleanup. Normalization still precedes the logged
gate, and the guard still spans status publication and log traversal. First
validated status, decisive failures and repeated-finalization behavior remain.

The sole production caller in pg_logging awaits finalize_ordinary_incomplete
before terminal logging. Response settlement and cleanup share the driver mutex,
and cleanup marks the processor finished. This lifecycle makes the removed
inter-lock window unnecessary; arbitrary concurrent call traces are not claimed
equivalent. No body owner, deadline, log contents or observability surface changes.
The benefit is one fewer mutex acquisition, without a measured throughput claim.

against unchanged production. Fresh serial verification passed all 27 Gateway

benchmark ran. JWKS/discovery snapshot Arcs remain necessary for caller ownership
outside provider state locks and were not replaced by borrowed cache references.

## Compute OIDC refresh coordination keys only when needed

Session authentication now starts with an empty request-local optional refresh
key. Cache-miss, preemptive and expired-token refresh branches initialize that
same slot on first use and reuse it thereafter. The digest still uses the
original encrypted cookie text, never a refreshed payload. Requests taking no
refresh branch avoid SHA-256 over the cookie and the Base64 output allocation.
Refresh predicates, timeout creation, flight/result-cache identity, cookie writes,
stale-token fallback and diagnostics remain unchanged. No shared cache or new
coordination mechanism was introduced.

Fresh verification passed 153 OIDC tests with 16 existing ignores, formatting,
workspace check/Clippy and seven repository guards with existing unrelated
warnings. Existing request tests seed results and occupy flights using the raw
cookie digest, alongside the stable-key and timeout regressions. Lazy computation
and reuse at all three sites are established by source dataflow, not a new
counter or an Option-internals test. No full suite or throughput benchmark ran.

## Avoid copying the token cleared from persisted OIDC sessions

Session-cookie publication now explicitly copies the six-field payload projection.
For a nonblank access token, the persisted projection starts with an empty token
and caches the original source bytes, avoiding the copy that was immediately
cleared. Empty and whitespace-only tokens preserve their previous representation
and skip cache insertion. Session-reference generation, remaining fields, TTL,
cache-before-cipher/size-check ordering and response append behavior are unchanged.
The input payload is not mutated; other field and cache-owned copies remain.

A six-case roundtrip matrix covers normal/empty/whitespace tokens with existing
or generated references, source immutability, all persisted fields and exact cache
contents. The original persistence test remains. Fresh verification passed 154
OIDC tests with 16 existing ignores, formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven
repository guards with existing unrelated warnings. This removes one temporary
nonblank access-token buffer, not encryption or serialized-cookie storage. No
full suite or throughput benchmark ran.

## Borrow the OIDC logout fallback target

Logout target selection now borrows immutable configured text or the static root
path. Building an IdP logout URL copies the fallback only when discovery has no
usable endpoint or endpoint parsing fails. Path-form post-logout URI expansion
formats the borrowed target directly; absolute URI results retain their owned
output. Prefix acceptance, Host/TLS derivation, query order, revocation, cookies
and response ownership remain unchanged. No lock is held by the borrowed target.

A focused test covers configured-pointer identity and the existing empty, relative,
absolute, case-sensitive and slash-prefix rules. Fresh verification passed 155
OIDC tests with 16 existing ignores, formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven
repository guards with existing unrelated warnings. This removes temporary target
copies, not the final redirect String. No full suite or throughput benchmark ran.

## Use fixed OIDC authorization random input arrays

Authorization state, optional nonce and optional PKCE verifier generation now use
const-sized 24/64-byte arrays instead of transient Vec buffers. All three call
sites retain their byte counts, RNG call order, ThreadRng fill_bytes operation and
URL-safe unpadded Base64 encoding. The encoded String remains owned. This removes
one input-buffer heap allocation per generated value, at the cost of small bounded
stack buffers and two generic instantiations; no measured speedup is claimed.

A protocol test constructs an authorization redirect and decrypts its state cookie,
checking query/cookie state and nonce identity, decoded byte counts, encoded lengths
and alphabet, original URL and the S256 challenge of the stored verifier. Existing
tests remain. Fresh verification passed 156 OIDC tests with 16 existing ignores,
formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven repository guards with existing
unrelated warnings. No full suite or throughput benchmark ran.

## Decode OIDC cookie nonces into a fixed array

Cookie decoding now uses the safe Base64 decode_slice API with a 12-byte nonce
array and checks its returned length. Valid nonce text reaches the same ciphertext
and AEAD stages; short, oversized or malformed nonce text still returns the fixed
MalformedCookie classification. Decoder details remain private. This removes the
nonce Vec allocation and bounds nonce output storage without changing ciphertext
storage, cookie encryption, JSON decoding or error projection.

Locked base64 0.22.1 uses the same internal decoder for both APIs; canonical
16-character nonce text fits the array exactly. Tests cover decoded lengths
0/1/11/12/13/64, padding, alphabet and trailing-bit failures, invalid ciphertext,
and a real encrypted cookie with a changed nonce returning InvalidCookieSignature.
Existing roundtrips remain. Fresh verification passed 157 OIDC tests with 16
existing ignores, formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven repository guards
with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite or throughput benchmark ran.

## Retain the default OIDC JWT required-claim set

OIDC JWT verification no longer replaces Validation::new's required-claim set
with another identical set containing exp. Locked jsonwebtoken 9.3.1 constructs
that set and owned claim name in new; the removed setter allocated replacements.
The per-verification Validation object and all issuer, audience, algorithm, time
and nonce policies remain unchanged. A source comment preserves the requirement
that exp remains mandatory even when expiration comparison is disabled.

A six-case real-signature test through the network-free scripted JWKS provider
covers missing/future/past exp with validate_exp enabled and disabled. Missing exp
still returns InvalidToken in both modes; expired tokens return Expired only when

tests with 16 existing ignores, formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven
repository guards with existing unrelated warnings. This removes redundant
HashSet/String construction, not all validation allocations. No full suite or
throughput benchmark ran.

jwk_matches_alg now compares KeyAlgorithm directly with an exhaustive mapping

## Reuse callback-local Guardrail remaining-byte accounting

Guardrail rollback reservation no longer rescans every remaining record and its

Identity-bound Service failure completion now stops counting open endpoint states

lock, service ejection lock and candidate revalidation remain unchanged.

AiCredentialOutlierBackendHandle::failure_allowed now limits its filtered

The request plugin decodes matching header/cookie tokens and calls verification.

change, including 63/65-byte rejection, exact-length invalid signatures, known
valid signatures and lifetime boundaries. Formatting, workspace all-target
check/Clippy and seven guards passed with existing unrelated warnings. No full
suite or throughput benchmark ran. The gain is avoiding cryptographic work only
for malformed lengths; it is not an allocation reduction claim.

Knowledge follow-up outside this batch: the typical CSRF example in
`skills/04-review/security/mandatory-design/iron-rules.md` assumes the nonce is
unknown to the caller. Here `CsrfToken::decode` obtains `random` from the supplied
token and verification uses those bytes. That rationale did not justify this optimization or establish exploitability.
The subsequent knowledge-correction batch below resolves this follow-up.
The owning signature-input knowledge now states the actual public-length proof.

## Passthrough SNI parsing and connection-owned name audit

In routes/tls/sni_parser.rs, extract_sni bounds the first ClientHello body by its
declared handshake length and validates extension and SNI-list container
boundaries before publishing a name. parse_sni_extension already borrows the
first host_name bytes without allocating. The first SNI extension remains
selected even if it contains no host_name; a later extension cannot repair it.
Returning immediately on the first hostname would skip malformed trailing
containers and change acceptance. This is structural validation, not full TLS
handshake validation.

Only after structural validation does the parser decode UTF-8 and use canonical
normalize_route_sni. Its into_owned result moves into TlsContext.sni. That owner
supports route/plugin work and disconnect logging after the inspection buffer
has been consumed and dropped by replay_initial_bytes. Returning a buffer borrow
would require a different lifetime design; it is not a disposable clone removal.
The parser receives record_end bytes, while replay keeps every filled byte,
including a coalesced tail. Neither boundary can replace the other.

No runtime edit is justified by this local audit. The existing
[ClientHello buffer-capacity proposal](tls-04-clienthello-buffer-capacity.md)
remains deferred. The authoritative
[ClientHello contract](../../skills/04-review/tls/regression-guards/sni-passthrough-clienthello-read.md)
still applies. Route-selection normalization, matcher internals and broader
transport dependencies are outside this completed parser inspection.

ResponseTrailerPolicy::capture runs only when the leased trailer companion list

## Request-body read and replay ownership audit boundaries

inspection borrows bytes; returned chunks retain shared ownership. Mirror

length only on timely success. Blocking closures retain their file/payload owners
through actual completion. Replay next_chunk does not consume its cursor; consume
advances it after delivery, while rewind captures the next immutable snapshot.

these boundaries. This inspection does not establish every OS scheduling order.

## WAF JSON structure ownership and duplicate lifecycle audit

Inspected the active JSON checker's structural path from bounded node/key/path
reservation through object insertion, duplicate replacement, sorted drain and
terminal cleanup, including json_scratch capacity arithmetic. This is bounded
structure-owner coverage, not complete lexer, collector, predicate or WAF review.

Incoming decoded keys are borrowed during lookup, then copied only for new object
members into a scoped key arena. Their identity must survive the token callback
for later duplicate lookup and sorted publication; dotted external path collisions
remain distinct from duplicate keys within one object. Duplicate insertion returns
without rewriting ancestor links/heights. The selected node's preceding receipt
is discarded before its subtree is reset; failures retain canonical abandonment.

Object completion drains the balanced key index in order before truncating node
and key arenas to the object's marks. Parent scopes remain live, while subsequent
siblings reuse retained capacities. The reducer's arrays retain frame summaries
and receipts rather than an element-value tape; this does not describe downstream
collector payload retention. Path storage is reused and restored by frame marks.
Node reads/writes and comparisons have explicit ordered work charges, so a Copy
operation is not authority to remove the corresponding budget step.

Complete-source node hints are enabled only when a conservative aggregate bound
fits. A hint is attempted at zero node capacity; reservation failure falls back
to ordinary demand growth, and successful allocation reconciles actual capacity.
Inline key/path bytes are excluded from heap usage; first spill charges the full
heap allocation through the canonical shared helper. Capacity reuse does not
refund live heap charges. Completion and failures release the structural owners;
feed retains the terminal result and does not publish partial failed receipts.

Independent plan review passed. No additional runtime optimization was selected.
Existing regressions exercise AVL rotations, decoded duplicates, nested scope
restoration, sibling reuse, conservative hints, exact/one-below physical limits,
malformed prefixes and callback failure cleanup. These are current implementation

## WAF result-store allocation and cleanup audit

Inspected json_inspection.rs record pools, BytePool, budget growth, receipt cleanup,
sealing and abandonment. Record slots reuse generational identities; removal
charges work before identity/generation checks and only then takes the value and
advances the slot. Parent-owner checks before removal retain distinct error order.

BytePool uses power-of-two small classes and page-rounded large classes. Small
heads are fixed; large-class metadata is sorted and its search/insertion is charged.
Freed blocks store the next free offset in their own bytes. Reuse retains backing
capacity; freeing logical payload does not refund allocated capacity or spent work.
Growth admits old storage plus a complete replacement, charges existing live bytes,
and checks actual allocator capacity. The optional page remainder falls back to
exact requested growth when its allowance is insufficient; unused spare bytes are
not initialized merely because capacity was reserved.

Shared outcome payloads retain whole-profile/candidate cleanup ownership. Sealing
builds qualified names only for surviving match views and resolves first named
values against compiled sorted demands. Sealed match/capture values remain opaque
handles into immutable request-owned storage. Dynamic owned values are separate.

An active operation failure invokes abandon before latching Failed. Eligible
abandonment drops owned pools and resets live usage while preserving spent work,
peak usage and externally owned scratch charges. Calls on already Abandoned or
Failed stores are no-ops. Scratch release remains the caller's responsibility after
its allocation is dropped; sealed replay budget failure is a separate sticky path.

The shared outbound loop now passes its remaining attempt count to

last permitted attempt takes it. A retry-capable call still rejects a streaming,

has been consumed. Backoff, deadlines, response caps, classification, passive
health and diagnostics retain their existing order.

## Terminal route metric handles and renewal gates

Traced pg_logging::record_request_metrics through route_handles, Common's metric
facade and dynamic Reference::slot/mutate. The prepared path borrows route,
gateway and backend identities, cached counter/histogram handles and admitted
slots. GatewayMatrixEntry validates both required slots before either write, so
an incomplete histogram slot does not increment a counter before dynamic fallback.
This is fallback safety, not a transaction spanning the two metric writes.

Prepared descriptors retain renewable proxies, not accumulation epochs. First
recording resolves admission; idle expiration removes the epoch without refunding
its admitted identity. A later event reuses that slot and initializes new values.
The warmed facade and slot lookup do not clone their retained handles. Short slot
gates protect the epoch while recording and updating its timestamp; expiry takes
an exclusive gate and rechecks age. Dropping an expired dense epoch happens after
the gate releases. Removing these gates merely because counters are atomic would
lose the lifetime/timestamp coordination.

No new safe optimization was selected. Dynamic fallback label capacity remains
tracked in metrics-01. This is a direct Gateway terminal-consumer and shared renewal
path inspection, not complete scrape rendering, admission/catalog, gauge-contribution
or metrics-system coverage. No shared crate code or ownership changed.

## Move mirror snapshot handles with stream state

The committed-snapshot stream now carries its budget, abandon reason and byte/
chunk counters alongside the reader in try_unfold's owned state. Each iteration
moves that state into its future and returns it with the next payload. This
removes five temporary Arc clone/drop pairs per iteration (two budget handles,
three atomics), including the terminal read. It does not remove the permit-owner
clones or independent payload copy required by try_copy, and claims no measured
throughput or stream-layout improvement.

EOF/error can drop these state handles before the stream itself is destroyed;
the handles own no permits. PreparedSnapshot and emitted BudgetedBytes retain
their existing separate charges, and the writer retains outcome/counter handles.
The locked futures-util 0.3.33 implementation owns either the idle state or the
pending future, so dropping a pending stream releases the reader and its charge.
No body storage, failure, counter ordering, cancellation or logging policy changed.

into the result. Previously it copied the payload into a temporary String and
then into a new Arc. The identity case now avoids both copies and their
nonempty-string allocations; empty strings also reuse the existing Arc.
Non-string values still use the canonical runtime_string conversion unchanged.
This is an identity fast path, not the deferred DSL 01 general coercion-owner
redesign. No throughput improvement was measured.

The length guard remains before return, and argument evaluation, value-work,
stack/call limits and error policy are unchanged. The complete immutable
Arc<str> is retained, without small-slice backing amplification.

Independent plan review passed. Baseline Gateway DSL verification passed 513
cases; final verification passed 514. Extended conversion tests cover ASCII,
multibyte and empty strings, repeated conversion and original-local reuse. A
new identity regression accepts four UTF-8 bytes at limit four and returns
exact StringTooLong { len: 4, limit: 3 } at limit three.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff
hygiene passed, with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite, live integration
or performance benchmark ran.

## Reuse range element formatting scratch

Range now formats each integer into one invocation-local String, clearing and
reusing its capacity before copying the text into each independent Arc<str>.
This replaces per-item temporary String construction with amortized scratch
growth. Empty ranges do not allocate scratch storage. Final list/Arc ownership,
standard decimal formatting, iteration order, checked subtraction/addition,
configured truncation and the 1000-element hard ceiling are unchanged.
No new formatter, dependency, logging or value-work accounting was introduced.
No exact allocation total or throughput improvement was measured.

Independent plan review passed. Baseline Gateway DSL verification passed 514
cases; final verification passed 515. The new regression retains earlier list

and i64::MAX - 1. Existing empty, overflow, indexing and truncation cases passed.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff

## Release serialized DSL body inputs before publication waits

JsonSetBody now drops its consumed source Arc after validation, budget admission
and copying into the independent outgoing Vec. XmlSetBody drops its consumed
XmlValue after bounded stringify produces the owned output String. Both releases
precede the canonical asynchronous overwrite_request_body call, whose adapter
can await replay-owner preparation.

This shortens input ownership across publication waits. Sole-owned JSON payloads
or XML tree allocations can be released earlier; locals and other shared aliases
remain owners, so no fixed freed-byte or throughput benefit is claimed. XML
nodes have no custom destructor, and output bytes no longer borrow either input.
All existing limits, work charges, allocation errors, validation order, body
publication/freeze behavior and error mappings remain unchanged.

Independent plan review passed. Baseline and final Gateway DSL verification
passed 515 cases, including existing JSON/XML publication, output failure,
rollback and frozen-generation coverage. No implementation-shaped lifetime test
or production visibility change was added. Formatting, workspace all-target
check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff hygiene passed, with existing
unrelated warnings. No full suite, live integration or performance benchmark ran.

## Release the consumed Body HMAC key before scanning

BodyHmacSha256 now moves its consumed Arc<str> into DslBodyOps. After the same
64-byte output preflight and owned HmacSha256Scanner construction, the facade
drops that Arc before awaiting the canonical scan. The scanner retains its
independent HMAC state, not a borrow of the original key.

This removes the current call's key owner across scan waits. Sole-owner payloads
can be reclaimed earlier; constants, locals or other aliases can still retain
them. This is neither zeroization nor a guaranteed heap/throughput reduction.
Strict key/Body validation, raw-byte hashing, output-limit precedence, scan
reservation/settlement and cancellation/worker ownership remain unchanged.

## Release temporary WAF heads after transaction publication

The Gateway WAF request callback now releases its temporary request-line,
normalized URI, raw URI and header-view Vec after successful transaction
construction. RequestState has already copied required bytes into its owned
arena/collections. The response callback similarly releases its header-view Vec
after successful publish_response_head builds the owned ResponseState.

Previously these locals remained in the callback drop scope during subsequent
rule execution, and request temporaries could remain across body-read waits.
Explicit drops shorten temporary retention without removing transaction-owned
copies or changing borrowed live headers. String and view carriers have no
custom destructor behavior. All drops precede the existing execution timer;

unchanged. No retained-byte accounting is refunded. No RSS or throughput

## Advance round-robin fallback without repeated remainder

RoundRobinSelector::select now increments the fallback index and resets it at
the backend-list boundary instead of calculating (primary + step) % count for
each candidate. The constructor bounds the list to u16::MAX slots, and the
weighted primary is a valid index, so the increment cannot overflow. The first
weighted remainder and single relaxed atomic cursor advance are unchanged.
The same loop range preserves the current zero-budget primary check, fallback
budget, candidate order and borrowed winner. No health result is cached or
predicate evaluation removed.

A differential test compares ordered predicate traces and pointer-identified
winners against the original modulo formula for every slot of a weighted
three-backend sequence, every health mask, boundary budgets and usize::MAX
cursor/budget values. It also verifies the wrapping cursor advance. Existing
empty/singleton, distribution, weighted fallback and truncation tests remain.

Independent plan review passed. Fresh baseline selection/compiled-selector
tests passed 40/8; final tests passed 41/8. Formatting, workspace all-target
check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff hygiene passed with existing
unrelated warnings. The removed source-level remainder is not a measured
throughput or latency improvement. No full suite, live integration or benchmark

## P2C live score reads and EWMA per-attempt factor reuse audit

Inspected select_p2c, LbBackend::conn/score and PeakEwmaScore's direct read/update
paths. P2C borrows candidates and clones only the winner. Its two-host second
index is deterministic; larger lists use the existing distinct-index mapping.
Each sampled pair reads live metrics before ordered health checks; retries can
sample a backend again and observe newer atomics. The final linear scan checks
health without scoring. Caching metrics across attempts would change those
observations, so no such runtime change was selected.

PeakEwmaScore::read projects one packed relaxed load without write-back. In
observe, decay_to_default and the faster-sample blend visibly call decay_parts
with the same elapsed value. An isolated optimized compilation of the current
source already merges that interpolation: the LLVM observe body computes q16
once and its blend block reuses q16 and whole-half-life values. Failed cmpxchg
returns to the loop and recalculates from the newly observed packed state.
Moving these values outside the CAS loop would violate the canonical estimator
invariant. No helper extraction or runtime refactor is justified by the apparent
duplicate source calls alone.

Reproduction from the repository root (temporary probe only):

```sh
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
source = Path('edgion-gateway/src/lb/ewma/score.rs').resolve()
Path('/tmp/edgion-ewma-observe-probe.rs').write_text(
    f'#[path = "{source}"] mod score;\n'
    '#[no_mangle]\n'
    'pub fn observe_probe(value: &score::PeakEwmaScore, sample: u32, now: u32) '
    '{ value.observe(sample, now); }\n'
)
PY
rustc --edition=2021 --crate-type lib -O --emit=llvm-ir /tmp/edgion-ewma-observe-probe.rs -o /tmp/edgion-ewma-observe-probe.ll
```

Observed with rustc 1.96.1 (31fca3adb), LLVM 22.1.2, host aarch64-apple-darwin.
Inspect the observe/observe_probe function bodies and the blend's use-def chain,
not merely the total division count across the module. This is isolated optimized
IR evidence, not a full Gateway release-binary inspection, CPU benchmark or
guarantee for other toolchains/targets. Re-evaluate if code or compilation changes.
The larger exact fractional table in [lb-01](lb-01-precomputed-ewma-decay.md)
remains deferred; common-expression elimination does not settle that tradeoff.

Independent plan review passed. Fresh tests passed 21 estimator, six P2C and
30 tests selected by lb::backend (three counter tests plus 27 BackendRef-selector
tests). No runtime code changed. This closes this scoped duplicate-computation
candidate, not rand internals, discovery, estimator policy tuning or full
contention/performance validation.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, agent-doc validation and diff
hygiene passed with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite or live
integration ran.

## ExtProc observable-verdict poll and partial-frame ownership

Traced ExtProcStream::reject_observable_unsolicited through the locked workspace
tonic 0.12.3 codec/decode.rs and futures-util 0.3.33 FutureExt::now_or_never.
The separately declared OTLP tonic 0.14 dependency is not this client. message()
borrows Streaming through poll_fn; now_or_never stack-pins that future and polls
once with a noop waker. There is no extra boxed message future to remove here.
Streaming owns decoder state, partial frame bytes, pending message length,
decompression scratch and trailers. Returning Pending and dropping this borrowed
future does not move those owners out of the stream.

This does not make the whole operation allocation-free or a single-frame poll:
tonic's poll_next loop can consume multiple ready frames, grow buffers and decode
an owned protobuf response before returning. The check rejects only an observable
complete verdict/error/EOF; it does not prove remote causality or detect a verdict
whose remaining bytes have not arrived. Replacing it with a different readiness
test could weaken the protocol boundary without eliminating the decoder's work.

Added a network-free production-branch regression using actual tonic Streaming,
ProstCodec and the existing Axum streaming Body over a controlled byte channel.
Independent streams split a nonempty gRPC message within the five-byte header,
at the header boundary and within the payload. Two pending checks retain state;
completing each frame produces the exact unsolicited-verdict rejection and sends
no outbound request. This extends the existing test-only receiver coverage; it
does not establish HTTP/2 interoperability, compression behavior or all transport
cancellation interleavings. No runtime code or dependency changed.

Independent plan review passed. Fresh client baseline passed 29 tests; final
ExtProc tests passed 147. Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, seven
repository guards and diff hygiene passed with existing unrelated warnings.
No full suite, live integration or performance benchmark ran. Revalidate the
source ownership proof and regression when the codec dependencies change.

leave proof publication available. This does not implement graphql-01 frontend
reuse or retain a parser owner, and does not change cache generation validation.

## Prepare RealIp header names at policy binding

RealIpPolicy now converts its canonically validated header name into HeaderName
once after trust-reference binding. The extractor stores this instead of its
String, and both plugin/current-map and global custom-header reads borrow it.
Global XFF selection compares normalized text and keeps the bounded aggregate
snapshot. No new header parser, trust view, schema or general session API is added.
This avoids repeated name processing; http's existing string lookup did not
allocate, so no request-allocation or measured throughput gain is claimed.

The existing isolated trusted-peer regression now exercises mixed-case standard
and custom names while retaining IP update and sensitive-log assertions. Baseline
and final selections each passed 34 Gateway RealIp, nine XFF snapshot and ten
Resources RealIp tests (53 executions). Initial compilation found an unavailable
header constant and one missed test constructor conversion; both were corrected
before the successful final run. Formatting, workspace check/Clippy and seven
repository guards passed with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite, live
network test or performance benchmark ran.

## RealIp canonical radix membership traversal

Traced policy membership through BoundIpPredicate and the captured ConfigData
reader into IpRadixMatcher and its frozen binary core. contains already selects
compile-time first-terminal traversal; group lookup retains longest-prefix matching.
The group API borrows the label while its Arc-returning sibling clones shared
ownership only when requested. RealIp membership does not project group text.

Native IPv4 and mapped IPv6 query only the IPv4 tree; other IPv6 queries only its
own tree. Query conversion remains numeric. The shared monomorphized core walks
at most 32/128 edges plus the root, guards bit-width before shifting, checks node
indices and uses DFS's nonzero-child/zero-sentinel invariant. It allocates no
collection, parses no CIDR, takes no lock and uses no runtime trait dispatch inside
the core. This does not remove surrounding PluginSession capability dispatch or
reference authorization/index lookup.

Existing layout, traversal-counter, nested-prefix and address-family tests cover
these boundaries. The canonical algorithm document already records 16-byte node
layout, construction costs and measured replacement criteria; no duplicate layout
task or runtime edit is selected. Decision-scoped lookup reuse remains ip-03, and
this audit does not claim every publication helper or policy consumer is complete.

Fresh selections passed 51 Algo radix-IP, 34 Gateway RealIp, 15 IP-reference and
22 ConfigData tests (122 executions across selections), formatting, workspace
check/Clippy and agent-doc validation with existing unrelated warnings. No new
layout, performance benchmark, full suite or live network verification ran.

The metadata helper now returns an absent over-limit snapshot as soon as checked

reverse that decision, so their iteration and text validation are skipped. The
single-field success path reuses its first text conversion. Admitted repeated
fields retain ordered separator accounting and the existing allocation boundary.
Invalid text below the cap still requires counting later fields; Host/path error
precedence, configured defaults, RealIp consumption and owned access-log state
remain unchanged. No throughput improvement is quantified.

The expanded existing boundary fixture covers zero limits, empty fields, exact

send_proxy_protocol_v2 now scopes its builder to header construction, releasing

Both terminate and passthrough handle_connection paths now drop last_err after

atomic cursor, modulo, selection ownership and all constructor guards remain.

plan review passed. No measured throughput or whole-constructor heap claim is made.

bound of target plus positive item count. GCD preserves ratios exactly; integer
scaling approximates them. The old weight-expansion fix remains valid, while
construction now belongs to route compilation and the old webhook caller is

and pre-await key release, cancellation ownership and error mapping are unchanged.
The buffers are initialized only after scanning completes and use the existing
hex encoder, whose fixed output size and ASCII alphabet justify the assertions.

## Compare body prefix and equality text by chunk slices

TextOperationScanner StartsWith and Equals now compare the relevant byte slices
instead of advancing their matched counter in a per-byte loop. StartsWith stops
on a mismatch or completed pattern; Equals continues on an exact chunk match
until EOF or later excess/mismatching text. No pattern ownership, preparation,
lossy decoder, scan worker or storage representation changes are included.

Each admitted push retains its Continue/Stop decision and final boolean. A failed
comparison no longer advances matched over its matching prefix, but that terminal
private count is unobservable: finish checks failed and LossyTextScanner never
feeds the inner scanner after Stop. Storage still charges the complete fetched
chunk before handling Stop, so scan accounting and budget granularity are unchanged.
This uses standard slice equality with no new allocation or unsafe code; no
throughput, vectorization or constant-time comparison claim is made.

same 14 test identities, including explicit chunk decisions and all three-way

normalized-path refresh; capture follows body preparation and precedes backend
modifiers/provider preparation. This isolation cannot be removed as a redundant
clone. The [deferred investigation](retry-03-ai-request-baseline-rebuild.md)

raw target and end-stream state; clone_from has no specialized reuse path. The
baseline owns no body copy, and cloned containers do not establish deep copying
of every payload. Ordinary endpoint retries are outside this decision.

## Reuse static AI candidate projections within one selection call

The synchronous select_target loop now initializes static RouteCandidate fields
once in its existing exact-capacity local Vec. Later backend scans update only
round exclusions and live adaptive snapshots, in declaration order. The immutable
candidate backend/model, credential weights and captured outlier-handle membership
do not change within this call; credential availability here tests handle presence,
not current health. Cost projection and repeated membership scans can therefore be
reused without retaining a cache in the request plan or changing admission policy.

Every new select_target call starts empty, including after model resolution or
quota downgrade outside this boundary. Direct credential selection and stopped
states retain lazy zero-allocation behavior. Picker validation, original slot
conversion, scheduler transitions and the existing within-call buffer capacity
remain unchanged. Adaptive reads occur on every scan; the first scan performs
static construction before those ordered reads, not a simultaneous telemetry
snapshot. No static fact is promoted into a live health/admission decision.

Independent investigation selected this bounded local change instead of requiring
an unnecessary publication/cache redesign. The implementation introduces no inline
stack buffer, new plan field or cross-call retained projection. Source-level work
removed is repeated static reconstruction on multi-scan calls; no throughput or
additional allocation reduction is claimed.

## Transfer the admission breaker owner into its permit

LogicalBackendCircuitBreaker::try_acquire now consumes its Arc and moves that
owner into the successful permit. AiAttemptRuntimeState::admit takes the existing
optional input owner instead of borrowing it and cloning again. The selected
policy generation is still cloned by prepared admission projection; that retained
source ownership remains necessary. Tests that retain a breaker explicitly clone
before acquiring rather than adding a second production API.

This removes one Arc increment/decrement on successful acquisition. It introduces
no allocation or measured throughput claim. The exact fetch_update, atomic
orderings, limit arithmetic and permit Drop are unchanged. Active/overflow,
breaker, outlier and Redis gate precedence remains intact. Rejections release the
local permit; successful runtime, predispatch teardown and cancelled admission
retain existing RAII ownership. The unrelated optional reservation-input decision
remains open and is not implemented by this transfer.

Independent plan review passed. A baseline-first actual admission test verifies
release after missing outlier, missing Redis dependency, dropping an uninstalled
runtime and predispatch finish. Breaker tests additionally cover exact-generation
sole ownership, zero-capacity denial and the u32 maximum boundary. Existing
aggregate-cap and dispatch skip/retry tests retain their assertions.
Final verification passed three breaker, 26 runtime and 39 dispatch tests
(68 total); runtime baseline and final retain the same 26 identities/outcomes.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff
hygiene passed with existing unrelated warnings. No full workspace test suite,

## Skip impossible duration parsing for absolute reset timestamps

The shared parse_rate_limit_reset helper now bypasses its duration attempt when
the trimmed input has a hyphen at byte four. GEP-2257 durations contain only
ASCII digits and h/m/s unit bytes, so such an input cannot succeed as a duration.
This is a negative discriminator, not a timestamp validator: the existing Chrono
RFC3339 parser still decides validity. Epoch parsing remains first; whitespace,
short/UTF-8 input safety, past-time zero, pre-epoch rejection and overflow behavior
are unchanged. Inputs without that separator retain the previous parser order.
Re-evaluate the discriminator if the canonical duration grammar changes.

The Gateway raw-response path reaches this shared helper through provider reset
hints after Retry-After fallback. The owning Common parser changes; no duplicate
Gateway grammar, error API, cache or header behavior is introduced. Independent
plan review approved this exact supporting cross-crate scope.

A baseline-first common test compares the full original parser chain across
valid/invalid duration forms, segment limits, epoch bounds, RFC3339 offsets and
fractional seconds, past/pre-epoch values, whitespace, short/multibyte inputs and
ASCII boundary bytes. A Gateway allocation test exercises both OpenAI reset-header
names with UTC, offset and fractional timestamps, preparing headers before counting.
It compares the original duration-then-timestamp fallback to provider_reset_hint
and requires equal parsed values. Existing unused-fallback and cooldown tests
remain unchanged. No throughput or full-hook allocation claim is made.
The measured timestamp fixtures each eliminate one allocation of the input byte
length; the current reset-header helper allocates zero in those fixtures. Other
malformed inputs can still allocate duration errors, and cooldown normalization
can allocate its output header. Final verification passed seven shared-time,
17 duration, seven response, 17 credential and 26 runtime tests (74 total).
The original/final shared-time runs have identical identities and outcomes.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy, seven repository guards and diff
hygiene passed with existing unrelated warnings. No full workspace test suite,
live provider exchange or throughput benchmark ran.

## Serialize model lists without intermediate JSON maps

The private AI model-list encoder now serializes two typed local structures.
Model IDs still move into the entry collection, while field names and fixed
`model`, `edgion` and `list` values no longer require owned JSON strings or maps.
The entry Vec and output buffer remain. Visibility, sorting, deduplication,
request snapshot ownership, failure handling, headers and write ordering stay
with their existing owners; no model-list cache or upstream aggregation is added.

Field declaration order matches the current sorted serde_json Map bytes:
`data, object` outside and `created, id, object, owned_by` inside. The current
Gateway dependency feature graph does not enable `preserve_order`. Exact-byte
regressions compare against both the original json! construction and the preceding
owned-Map encoder, covering empty lists, escaped/multibyte IDs and larger lists.
A future serde_json feature change must retain or explicitly revisit these tests;
no alternate-feature build is claimed.

The original 22 proxy tests passed before editing. Final verification passed 23
proxy and four model-router tests. An isolated encoder comparison for zero, one,
16 and 128 entries showed fewer allocation calls and fewer cumulative requested
bytes in every case, with input construction/cloning outside the counters. This
is not a throughput, peak-memory or whole-request allocation measurement.
Formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy and seven repository guards passed
with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite or live integration test ran.

## Borrow native Messages kind discriminators

The private native Messages `kind` projection now reuses the canonical borrowed
JSON string decoder. Unescaped type/fallback discriminators borrow their original
RawValue text; escaped strings still decode into owned values. All consumers are
local equality or prefix checks. Model ownership, body bytes, selective parsing,
nested traversal and existing error wrapping remain unchanged.

Null filtering and the 386-byte encoded limit still run before decoding. A frozen
old-decoder oracle verifies missing/null values, wrong JSON types, plain and
escaped strings, permitted multibyte text, encoded-size boundaries, oversized
non-string values and invalid surrogate tokens where RawValue admits them.
Nested escaped tool-result/file and tool-addition/advisor fixtures preserve both
binding and composite detection. Nine tests passed against the old implementation
before the production edit; an initial test-only Result comparison compile error
was corrected before that successful baseline.

The allocation regression verifies source-pointer identity and zero decoder
allocations for four nonempty unescaped discriminators whose old String decoder
allocated. Escaped text remains owned with equal decoded content. These counters
exclude fixture construction and do not measure complete metadata parsing,
request throughput or retained heap. No new parser, cache, log or metric is added.
Fresh final verification passed ten native request, five shared JSON span and 23
AI proxy tests (38 total), formatting, workspace all-target check/Clippy and seven
repository guards with existing unrelated warnings. No full suite, alternate
feature build or live-provider test ran.

## Borrow decoded model names during native rewrite comparison

The shared native model decoder now returns a Cow through the existing canonical
borrowed JSON string decoder. Chat and Messages rewrite comparisons borrow plain
model text instead of allocating a temporary String. Escaped names remain owned.
Chat, Responses and Messages metadata explicitly convert the result into their
existing owned String at the same ownership boundary; no borrowed value is
retained in request plans or response processors.

Validation order is unchanged: missing field, non-string type, encoded-size cap,
JSON decoding, then nonempty/decoded UTF-8 byte cap. Replacement serialization,
span calculation and body patching remain unchanged. This does not cache parsed
request metadata, avoid complete native UTF-8/syntax checks, or alter canonical
BodyStorage generations.

Four shared tests passed before the production edit, including a frozen old
decoder oracle at encoded/decoded limits, multibyte names, oversized nonstrings,
and invalid surrogates where RawValue admits them. Both native rewrite adapters
preserve escaped equality and exact unrelated bytes during a changed-model edit.
The final allocation regressions check original-pointer borrowing for plain names
and actual unchanged-model Chat/Messages calls on one prebuilt fixture. These
measure only the named decoder/call cases; they do not establish zero allocation
for arbitrary request documents or a throughput improvement.
